title: Introduce slim-safeguard defaults mapper and quantization rollback hooks
author: Maya L. Cohen
release_notes: Adds a defaults mapper service that produces conservative batching and caching defaults per-tenant and a quantization rollback hook that integrates with telemetry and the Console. No public API changes.
description: Context: Customers run into intermittent quality regressions after deploying aggressive quantized variants; teams also ask for safer per-tenant defaults for batching and cache residency. This PR introduces a new 'slim-safeguard' defaults-mapper microservice and a quantization rollback hook that can automatically evaluate recent model rollouts against unit-econ and quality smoke gates. Motivation: reduce manual toil when tuning tenant defaults, prevent silent quality drops from small quantization changes, and provide an automated conservative fallback so customer applications remain within unit-econ and latency SLOs. What this change does: 1) Defaults mapper: a lightweight service that synthesizes per-tenant conservative defaults for batch_size, kv_cache_retention, and prefill_window based on recent traffic histograms and latency headroom. It emits suggestions to the defaults API and the Console preview UI. 2) Quant rollback hooks: on a quantized model rollout, the platform runs a quick regression probe (unit-econ smoke + eval against a short prompt set) and, on regression above threshold, triggers a rollback policy or a soft-fallback (route to non-quant variant for N minutes). 3) Integration and telemetry: new telemetry tags (safeguard.tenant_hint, quant.rollback_reason) and metrics for hit-rate, rollback_count, and suggested_defaults_applied. 4) Safety toggles: experimental flag in tenant defaults and an operator CL that allows dry-run and manual-approve flows. Backwards compatibility: existing APIs unchanged; all changes behind feature flag 'safeguard.defaults' by default off for tenants. Checklist: - [x] defaults-mapper service and API adapters - [x] quick regression probe harness and eval set - [x] Console preview and opt-in toggle - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] documentation for operators and SRE - [x] smoke test in canary cluster Implementation notes: This is intentionally conservative. The defaults mapper prefers lower batch sizes when tail latency is within 10% of SLA and recommends cache reductions only if cold-start cost dominates. Rollback hook uses a weighted-signal aggregator across unit-econ delta and model-quality delta and requires a 2/3 quorum from quality signals before triggering automated rollback. Related: ENG-1421 (defaults automation), ENG-1890 (quant-safety roadmap), SUP-887 (customer incident that motivated the change). How to test: run ./dev/ci/safeguard_smoke.sh against a local canary image; the script exercises a synthetic tenant workload and simulates a quantized rollout. See notes_on_testing. Migration: operator can enable the feature flag per-tenant; we provide a one-click preview in Console. Rollouts and observed metrics will inform whether suggested defaults are applied automatically or kept as suggestions.

notes_on_testing: The smoke harness (tests/smoke/safeguard_smoke.sh) starts a local canary of defaults-mapper, deploys a synthetic tenant that emits a 90:10 short:long request mix and then triggers a quantized rollout. The harness validates: no more than 2% quality regression on eval set, unit-econ delta under configured threshold, and operator notification created. The canary job is configured in CI as canary/safeguard and runs on every release candidate when the feature-flag image tag is present.
motivation_summary: Automate conservative defaults and protect against accidental quality regressions from quantization changes to reduce operator toil and reduce P1 incidents for customers.
